categories.label: Razorpay-native mechanic
categories.description: A documented payment or settlement lifecycle behavior reproduced with simulated money.

categories.label: Cross-system integration failure
categories.description: A plausible bank, ERP, export, pagination, or ETL discrepancy—not asserted to be emitted by Razorpay.

categories.label: Adversarial stress case

categories.label: ERP control / fraud anomaly
categories.description: A plausible merchant-control pattern requiring independent ERP, approval, or vendor-master evidence.

settlement_cycle.label: Working-day settlement cycle
settlement_cycle.realism_basis: Razorpay documents working-day settlement cycles whose exact schedule varies by merchant and product.
settlement_cycle.frequency_note: Routine lifecycle behavior; the demo's Monday-Friday calendar is simplified.
settlement_cycle.claim_boundary: The synthetic T+1/T+2 mix is a policy fixture, not a universal merchant contract.

settlement_components.label: Net settlement components
settlement_components.realism_basis: A bank settlement can be the net result of captured payments and deductions such as fees or refunds.
settlement_components.claim_boundary: Only the component arithmetic is represented; production product configuration can differ.

partial_settlement.label: Partial settlement
partial_settlement.realism_basis: Razorpay documents partial settlement behavior when available live balance is below the scheduled amount.
partial_settlement.frequency_note: Possible lifecycle behavior rather than an anomaly by itself.
partial_settlement.claim_boundary: The demo does not infer merchant eligibility or actual settlement configuration.

benign_one_day_posting_lag.label: Benign posting lag
benign_one_day_posting_lag.realism_basis: Bank posting and settlement timestamps can cross business-day boundaries.
benign_one_day_posting_lag.claim_boundary: A lag is not fraud and should not be flagged without contradictory evidence.

amount_mismatch.label: Amount mismatch
amount_mismatch.realism_basis: The bank amount disagrees with the independently recomputed settlement net.
amount_mismatch.frequency_note: Plausible ingestion, mapping, adjustment, or accounting exception.
amount_mismatch.claim_boundary: The demo does not claim Razorpay generated the incorrect value.

duplicate_reference.label: Duplicate reference
duplicate_reference.realism_basis: The same external reference appears on multiple economic events or imports.
duplicate_reference.frequency_note: Plausible duplicate-file, replay, manual-entry, or upstream-reference issue.
duplicate_reference.claim_boundary: A duplicate reference is a review signal, not proof of provider or customer fraud.

unsupported_transaction.label: Unsupported transaction
unsupported_transaction.realism_basis: A bank movement lacks independent operational support in the supplied systems.
unsupported_transaction.frequency_note: Common reconciliation exception when feeds are late, incomplete, or mapped incorrectly.
unsupported_transaction.claim_boundary: Absence in a simulated extract is not proof the real transaction is unauthorized.

unattributed_settlement_component.label: Unattributed settlement component
unattributed_settlement_component.realism_basis: The settlement balances, but one adjustment cannot be attributed to an independent source record.
unattributed_settlement_component.frequency_note: Plausible close-control exception caused by incomplete component evidence.
unattributed_settlement_component.claim_boundary: The controller refuses component closure; it does not label the adjustment fraudulent.

balance_rollforward_mismatch.label: Balance roll-forward mismatch
balance_rollforward_mismatch.realism_basis: A statement row does not reconcile to the previous running balance.
balance_rollforward_mismatch.frequency_note: Plausible export corruption, missing row, sign error, or ingestion-order defect.
balance_rollforward_mismatch.claim_boundary: This is a bank-data integrity check, not a Razorpay-native anomaly.

counterparty_substitution.label: Counterparty substitution
counterparty_substitution.realism_basis: Money and reference can agree while the observed payee identity conflicts with approved merchant evidence.
counterparty_substitution.frequency_note: Plausible control breach, data-entry error, or beneficiary substitution pattern.
counterparty_substitution.claim_boundary: Razorpay settlement data alone cannot establish this; independent ERP evidence is required.

collusive_duplicate.label: Collusive duplicate
collusive_duplicate.realism_basis: A new-looking reference and approval can still repeat an earlier economic amount/counterparty motif.
collusive_duplicate.frequency_note: Plausible duplicate-payment or collusion control scenario.
collusive_duplicate.claim_boundary: The graph signal only requests review and cannot prove intent or collusion.

approver_velocity_burst.label: Approver velocity burst
approver_velocity_burst.realism_basis: One approver authorizes an unusual cluster of events in a short period.
approver_velocity_burst.frequency_note: Plausible behavioral-control signal with legitimate end-of-period alternatives.
approver_velocity_burst.claim_boundary: Velocity requires historical context and is never fraud proof by itself.

structured_split_payment.label: Structured split payment
structured_split_payment.realism_basis: Related payments are divided into smaller events that may avoid a control threshold.
structured_split_payment.frequency_note: Plausible control-circumvention pattern with legitimate installment alternatives.
structured_split_payment.claim_boundary: The required linkage is unavailable from Razorpay settlement data alone.

coordinated_vendor_master_takeover.label: Vendor-master takeover
coordinated_vendor_master_takeover.realism_basis: A beneficiary change precedes coordinated payments to the modified vendor identity.
coordinated_vendor_master_takeover.claim_boundary: Detection requires independent, timestamped vendor-master evidence not present in a normal settlement export.

out_of_hours_approval.label: Out-of-hours approval
out_of_hours_approval.realism_basis: An approval occurs outside the declared operating calendar.
out_of_hours_approval.frequency_note: Plausible weak signal with many benign explanations.
out_of_hours_approval.claim_boundary: Operating-hours deviation must be combined with stronger evidence before escalation.

benign_uncommon_operating_path.label: Benign uncommon operating path
benign_uncommon_operating_path.realism_basis: An uncommon but legitimate path is included as a hard negative.
benign_uncommon_operating_path.frequency_note: Necessary to measure false-positive cost around rare behavior.
benign_uncommon_operating_path.claim_boundary: Uncommon does not mean dubious; this row must remain unflagged.

topology:1:1.label: One bank entry → one settlement
topology:1:1.frequency_note: Expected primary topology in a clean direct settlement feed.
topology:1:1.claim_boundary: Its presence is realistic; the demo does not estimate its production share.

topology:1:N.label: One bank entry → many settlements
topology:1:N.realism_basis: Possible when an external bank or treasury layer aggregates separately identified settlements.
topology:1:N.frequency_note: Plausible cross-system shape, but not asserted as standard Razorpay settlement behavior.
topology:1:N.claim_boundary: Included to prove grouped reconciliation, not to model production frequency.

topology:N:1.label: Many bank entries → one settlement
topology:N:1.realism_basis: Possible when posting, partial-credit, retry, or intermediate-ledger behavior splits one economic settlement.
topology:N:1.frequency_note: Adversarial integration topology rather than the expected clean path.
topology:N:1.claim_boundary: Included to test global grouping; actual frequency is unknown.

topology:N:M.label: Many bank entries ↔ many settlements
topology:N:M.realism_basis: A bounded netting or aggregation layer can create an irreducible many-to-many explanation.
topology:N:M.frequency_note: High-complexity stress case and not claimed as a routine native feed shape.
topology:N:M.claim_boundary: The balanced demo count deliberately over-samples this topology.
